executive_summary: The Swedish krona enters September 2026 at the weak extreme of its twelve-month range on every measure that matters. USD/SEK closed at 9.57776 and EUR/SEK at 11.12656 on 31 August 2026, the latter at the 100th percentile of its 52-week close distribution, and the Riksbank's own KIX trade-weighted index finished the month at 120.20199 before printing 120.22986 on 1 September, up 3.92 per cent this year and roughly 3.5 per cent weaker than the 116.18 annual average the Riksbank assumed in its June Monetary Policy Report. Over one month the krona lost 0.59 per cent against the dollar, 1.33 per cent against the euro and 1.95 per cent against the Norwegian krone; over six months it lost 4.30 per cent, 4.42 per cent and 7.05 per cent against the same three; over twelve months it is 2.96 per cent weaker against the dollar and 8.76 per cent weaker against the krone. The dominant narrative is a relative-policy one: the Riksbank has now held at 1.75 per cent for seven consecutive meetings while the European Central Bank is more than 95 per cent priced to hike on 10 September and the Federal Reserve has repriced hawkishly, so the differential moved against the krona all summer even as Swedish activity data improved sharply. On valuation the krona is genuinely cheap - a BIS real effective rate of 96.46 for June 2026 at the 37th percentile of its window, and 10.55 per cent below the dollar and 6.07 per cent below the euro on a REER-relative basis - but cheapness has not paid for three quarters and the corroborated sell-side targets of 10.45 to 10.50 for end-2026 now sit roughly six per cent through spot. The central tension is that measured Swedish inflation understates the underlying rate by about 1.5 percentage points: CPIF printed 0.7 per cent in July, but adjusted for temporary fiscal measures the Riksbank itself puts it at 2.2 per cent, with second-quarter GDP at plus 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter and plus 3.3 per cent year on year against a June forecast of 2.2 per cent for the whole of 2026, and Governor Thedeen stating in the August minutes that the next change in the policy rate needs to be a rise. Against that stands a live terms-of-trade shock - Brent settled at 94.65 dollars and Dutch TTF gas reached about 70 euros a megawatt hour, its highest since January 2023 - which has collapsed the January-to-July goods surplus from SEK 51.4 billion to SEK 8.5 billion, a general election on 13 September, and a fiscal package that will not be revealed until roughly mid-November. The stance is Neutral tactically with conviction 2, because the September calendar front-loads the euro-positive event and back-loads the krona-positive one, and Bullish strategically with conviction 2 on a weighted score of plus 0.1605, with the explicit caveat that the strategic case rests almost entirely on the Riksbank delivering the hike its own Governor has signposted.

valuation.trade_weighted_assessment: On the Riksbank's own KIX measure the krona is 3.92 per cent weaker year to date and, at 120.20, roughly 3.5 per cent weaker than the 116.18 annual average the June Monetary Policy Report assumed. That is a material miss on the Riksbank's own import-weighted input, and it is the single most policy-relevant valuation number in this dossier: a weaker KIX than assumed mechanically raises the Riksbank's imported-inflation forecast and therefore its September rate path. The National Institute of Economic Research forecast KIX annual averages of 117.1 for 2026 and 117.6 for 2027 in its June vintage; spot is already 2.6 per cent weaker than the 2026 figure.
valuation.what_is_priced_in: The market is pricing the krona as a low-carry, low-liquidity currency in a live energy shock, and it is pricing very little of the Riksbank's own hawkish signalling. Roughly one 25 basis point hike is priced by end-2026, which is consistent with the June path but not with a board on which four of five members lean hawkish and the Governor has said the next move is a rise. What is emphatically NOT priced is a September rate-path upgrade driven by the KIX overshoot and a second-quarter GDP print that beat the Riksbank's own annual forecast in a single quarter.
valuation.actionability: The valuation signal is structural rather than tactical: a 37th-percentile real effective rate is a reason to prefer owning the krona over a six-month horizon, not a reason to buy it into a general election eleven days away. Cheapness has been true and unrewarded for three quarters, so it should be treated as a condition that improves the payoff of a catalyst rather than as a catalyst itself.

positioning_summary.other_positioning_signals: Three proxies carry real information. First, the Riksbank's own Financial Markets Survey for spring 2026, fielded 30 March to 17 April, found that market participants had reduced risk-taking versus autumn 2025 and attributed that primarily to the war in the Middle East; two-thirds judged the krona FX market to be functioning well, and liquidity in spot, forward and swap SEK was described as good but slightly deteriorated over the preceding six months. Second, CME lists no Swedish krona OPTIONS at all - the exchange's official FX options trading codes table covers only AUD, GBP, CAD, EUR, JPY, CHF and CNH - so there is no exchange-based skew or options-implied positioning read either. Third, and most durable, the Swedish institutional base is structurally short the krona: AP7, the default premium-pension fund, does not normally hedge its foreign currency exposure and cited krona strength against the dollar as the main drag on its 2025 return of 4.2 per cent, while the AP1 to AP4 buffer funds operate under a statutory limit on currency exposure that forces partial hedging. Krona strength mechanically hurts domestic institutional returns, which creates a slow-moving hedging reaction function rather than a fast speculative one.
positioning_summary.interpretation: Positioning must be inferred from price and from the shape of the forecast distribution rather than measured. Both point the same way: EUR/SEK at the 100th percentile of its 52-week close distribution, NOK/SEK at the 100th and within 20 pips of its high, and AUD/SEK at the 98th, while the corroborated sell-side targets for end-2026 sit at 10.45 and 10.50, roughly six per cent through spot. A market that is short a currency and simultaneously publishing bullish year-end targets on it is a market that has capitulated on timing but not on thesis.
positioning_summary.contrarian_assessment: The contrarian case is unusually clean precisely because the positioning data are absent. Every corroborated numeric forecast in the set - SEB at 10.45 and Bank of America at 10.50 for end-2026 - implies a krona rally that has not started, Nordea downgraded its conviction on 14 August while still calling the krona undervalued, and Rabobank has retreated to a range call. When the published consensus is stale-bullish and spot is at a range extreme in the other direction, the pain trade is a krona rally, and the 24 September Monetary Policy Report is the single most plausible trigger for one. The counter-argument is that a currency can stay at a range extreme for a long time when the flow story - an energy import bill and an unhedged domestic institutional base - is structural rather than speculative.

Low realised volatility at a range extreme with five scheduled binary events inside three weeks is an asymmetric configuration, and the fact that it cannot be priced against implied volatility is a genuine analytical loss rather than a formality.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime since June has been one of relative monetary policy overwhelming relative fundamentals. Swedish activity data improved markedly over the summer - second-quarter GDP at plus 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter, manufacturing PMI at 56.1 in August, household confidence back to normal for the first time since November 2024 - while the krona fell, because the Riksbank held for a seventh consecutive meeting as the ECB moved toward a September hike and the Fed repriced hawkishly. Overlaid on that is a live US-Iran conflict with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, which pushed Brent to a 94.65 dollar settlement and Dutch TTF gas to about 70 euros a megawatt hour, a direct terms-of-trade tax on a net energy importer that has collapsed the January-to-July goods surplus from SEK 51.4 billion to SEK 8.5 billion. The tell of the month is that the krona weakened while the broad dollar index fell 2.04 points and the VIX fell 6.23 points - the currency did not capture a risk-on, weak-dollar backdrop that historically flatters it, which says the marginal seller is responding to the rate differential and the import bill rather than to global risk appetite.

tactical.analysis: The tactical policy picture is genuinely two-sided, and that is why it scores Neutral at the heaviest weight in the framework. The level of Swedish carry is punishing: at 1.75 per cent the Riksbank runs the third lowest policy rate in the G10 and the krona is out-yielded by seven of the nine peers with a policy rate, by 260 basis points against Australia, 250 against Norway, 200 against the United Kingdom and 187.5 against the United States. Against that, the direction of Swedish rates is the most hawkish in the developed world relative to what is priced: Governor Thedeen told the 19 August meeting that he assesses that the next change in the policy rate needs to be a rise, Deputy Governor Seim said it may be necessary to raise during the autumn, and First Deputy Governor Bunge argued the rate should move from somewhat stimulating toward neutral. The Riksbank's own Markets Department told the board that market pricing had shifted upwards since June and was pricing just over one 25 basis point increase towards the end of 2026, which is marginally ABOVE the roughly 50 per cent probability embedded in the June path. The Swedish curve has already done some of this work: the two-year yield is 2.53 per cent as at 31 August, up 13.1 basis points on the month and 66.5 over twelve months, and the ten-year is 3.134 per cent, up 35.3 basis points since the cached 1 June monthly reading of 2.781 per cent and the highest since October 2023. The decisive tactical problem is sequencing. The European Central Bank meets on 10 September with more than 95 per cent priced for a 25 basis point hike to 2.50 per cent, which mechanically widens the krona's euro disadvantage from 50 to 75 basis points; the Riksbank does not meet until 24 September. For fourteen of the next twenty-two trading days the differential moves against the krona on the calendar alone, and the FOMC on 16 September carries a hawkish rather than dovish risk given three regional presidents dissented for a hike on 29 July. The offsetting tactical fact is that the 24 September Monetary Policy Report is a full forecast round in which the Riksbank must mark to market a second-quarter GDP print of plus 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter and plus 3.3 per cent year on year against an annual 2026 forecast of 2.2 per cent, and a KIX index 3.5 per cent weaker than the 116.18 it assumed. Both revisions push the published path up. strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the policy factor turns clearly krona-positive, because the level of carry stops being the binding constraint and the direction of the differential starts to be. Sweden is one of very few developed economies where the central bank's own published path is rising, where four of five voting members lean hawkish, and where the real policy rate is negative on the measure the central bank itself says it is watching. Adjusted for temporary fiscal measures the Riksbank puts July CPIF at approximately 2.2 per cent and CPIF excluding energy at approximately 1.6 per cent, so a 1.75 per cent policy rate is at or below the underlying inflation rate - a genuinely stimulative setting in an economy growing 3.3 per cent year on year with manufacturing PMI at 56.1. Deputy Governor Hjelm described the risk outlook as still asymmetrical with the risk of inflation becoming too high being dominant, and warned that an escalation with major price effects could entail much larger policy rate increases than the June path implies. Even Per Jansson, the most dovish member, hedged that if the bank fell behind the curve it could catch up with a few early rate increases in larger steps than the usual 0.25 percentage points - which is a dove pricing tail risk, not ruling it out. Meanwhile the peers that out-yield the krona are mostly at or past their peaks: Norges Bank at 4.25 per cent has room to cut as Norwegian disinflation proceeds, the RBNZ's easing bias is exhausted at 2.50 per cent, the Bank of Canada is done at 2.25 per cent, and the Bank of England has a gradual easing bias from 3.75 per cent. On six-month forward differentials the krona's disadvantage narrows against Norway, Britain, Canada and New Zealand, and widens materially only against the euro area. The bond market has already begun to price this: Sweden yields 131.4 basis points less than Norway at ten years against a 250 basis point policy gap, so roughly half the Scandinavian divergence is expected to close inside the forecast horizon, and the Swedish ten-year has risen 35.3 basis points in a quarter to its highest since October 2023. The strategic case is that the currency has not yet priced what the curve has.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: The split is mechanical and calendar-driven rather than analytical. Both horizons share the same view of the Riksbank's reaction function; they differ because within four weeks the euro-area hike lands on 10 September and the Swedish path revision lands on 24 September, so the differential moves against the krona for two-thirds of the tactical window before it can move for it. Over one to six months that sequencing washes out and what remains is the direction of the differential, which favours the krona against six of the nine peers with a policy rate. Confidence is only marginally higher strategically because the entire strategic case rests on a single institution delivering what it has signposted, and the Riksbank has now signposted without delivering for seven consecutive meetings.

carry_analysis.carry_regime: Carry has been working, and it has been working against the krona all year: the three worst krona crosses over twelve months - AUD/SEK plus 10.83 per cent, NOK/SEK plus 8.76 per cent and GBP/SEK plus 2.75 per cent - are precisely the three widest negative differentials, and all three sit at or above the 97th percentile of their 52-week close distributions. The regime's vulnerability is that it is now fully expressed. Carry regimes end not when the level of carry is unattractive but when its direction turns, and the direction turns on 24 September if the Riksbank upgrades its path while Norges Bank, the RBNZ and the Bank of Canada stand still at or past their peaks.

tactical.analysis: This is the factor carrying the tactical case, and it rests on a distinction that the headline data actively conceal. Measured Swedish inflation looks moribund: CPI rose just 0.2 per cent year on year in July 2026 and CPIF, the Riksbank's target measure, 0.7 per cent, down from 1.3 per cent in June and 3.0 per cent a year earlier. But the Riksbank's own June Monetary Policy Report states that temporary fiscal measures - a halved food VAT, a temporary fuel duty cut, halved public transport passes, reduced preschool fees - are depressing CPIF by as much as 1.5 percentage points in the third quarter of 2026, and at the 19 August meeting board members put July CPIF adjusted for those measures at approximately 2.2 per cent and CPIF excluding energy at approximately 1.6 per cent. On the measure the central bank actually targets, adjusted for distortions it created itself, Swedish inflation is at target and rising, not 1.3 percentage points below it. The growth side is unambiguous. Second-quarter GDP grew 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter seasonally adjusted and 3.3 per cent year on year calendar adjusted, revised up from the 29 July flash of 1.4 per cent, with gross fixed capital formation up 3.5 per cent and manufacturing value added up 7.1 per cent year on year. That single quarter exceeded the 2.2 per cent the Riksbank forecast for the whole of 2026 in June. Survey data confirm rather than contradict it: the Swedbank/Silf manufacturing PMI rose to 56.1 in August from 55.7, a fourteenth consecutive month above its 54.3 historical average, the NIER Economic Tendency Indicator rose for a fourth consecutive month to 105.1, retail confidence at 114.2 is the highest since early 2022, and household confidence returned to a normal 98.0 for the first time since November 2024. Cost pressure is re-accelerating from the supply side: the manufacturing PMI input-price index jumped to 75.4 from 67.1, and NIER shows manufacturing domestic selling-price plans at a net balance of 34 against a mean of 12. The 14 September August CPI print is the tactical trigger, with Danske forecasting CPIF at 1.00 per cent and CPIF excluding energy at 0.74 per cent - a rise from July on both.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market is trading the measured CPIF of 0.7 per cent, not the fiscally-adjusted 2.2 per cent, and it is treating Swedish disinflation as a reason the Riksbank can stay on hold indefinitely. That is a misreading of a central bank that has told the market in writing which number it is looking at. Our expectation is that the 14 September August print comes in at or above Danske's 1.00 per cent CPIF and that the 24 September Monetary Policy Report revises 2026 growth up sharply from 2.2 per cent, and that the combination forces a hawkish repricing of the front end that the currency has not begun to anticipate.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the inflation and growth configuration is the strongest in the G10 relative to the policy rate attached to it. Sweden is running 3.3 per cent year-on-year growth with a 1.75 per cent policy rate; the United States runs 2.1 per cent growth at 3.625 per cent, the euro area 1.0 per cent at 2.25 per cent and the United Kingdom 1.17 per cent at 3.75 per cent. On any Taylor-type reading Sweden is the most obviously under-tightened economy in the developed world once the fiscal distortion to its inflation measure is removed. The distortion itself is a dated, quantified and reversing phenomenon rather than a matter of judgement: the June Monetary Policy Report says the drag peaks at about 1.5 percentage points in the third quarter of 2026, unwinds from mid-2027 to end-2028 and then adds about 0.8 percentage points. The Riksbank's own June forecast has CPIF excluding energy and the direct effects of temporary measures rising from just over 1 per cent to as much as approximately 2.5 per cent during the spring of 2027. The counterweight is a labour market with genuine slack, and it is a real one: the Labour Force Survey seasonally adjusted trend rate is 8.7 per cent, the highest in the G10 by a wide margin, with youth unemployment at 24.4 per cent seasonally adjusted. That said, the register-based measures tell a better story - Arbetsforlmedlingen registered unemployment is 6.5 per cent and falling, and Statistics Sweden's register-based BAS measure is 5.1 per cent in June and has fallen for six to seven consecutive months - and about a third of the survey's unemployed are full-time students. Wage growth at 3.7 per cent against a 3.0 per cent contract implies positive wage drift, real wages are rising 2.4 per cent on CPIF, and the current agreement expires 31 March 2027, putting the next bargaining round just beyond the strategic horizon. The combination of accelerating activity, reversing fiscal drag and firm wage growth is a durably krona-positive inflation configuration.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Both horizons are Bullish and the difference in confidence is small and deliberate. Tactical confidence is marginally higher at 62 because there is a dated, near-term test - the 14 September August CPI print and the 24 September forecast round - that can confirm the view inside four weeks, whereas the strategic case depends on a fiscal reversal that does not begin until mid-2027. The strategic horizon also carries more of the labour-market risk: 8.7 per cent survey unemployment is a slow variable that could keep the Riksbank cautious for longer than the inflation data alone would justify. tactical.analysis: The global risk backdrop is objectively supportive and the krona is conspicuously failing to capture it, which is why this factor is Neutral rather than Bullish despite benign inputs. The VIX closed at 14.43 on 28 August 2026, down 6.23 points from 20.66 a month earlier and firmly in the lowest quartile of its post-2020 distribution. US investment-grade credit spreads are 79 basis points and high-yield 260 basis points, tighter by 27 basis points on the month, which is a tight-credit, low-volatility regime. Equities corroborate: the S&P 500 closed at 7,686.14 on 31 August, up about 12.5 per cent year to date, the Euro Stoxx 50 is up 20.6 per cent year on year and the OMX Stockholm 30 is up 26.9 per cent year on year, having set an all-time high of 3,349.20 in early August. The krona is supposed to be a European-beta, mildly risk-on currency: on the currency brief's own correlation table SEK versus the VIX runs minus 0.2 to minus 0.4, so a six-point VIX decline should have been worth something. It was worth nothing. The KIX index rose 1.12 per cent in August, on 14 of 21 sessions, and closed the month at its high. That correlation breakdown is the single most important observation in this factor and it cuts both ways: it says the standard risk transmission is not currently the marginal driver, so a further risk rally should not be assumed to help the krona, and equally that a risk selloff may hurt it less than the historical beta implies because the currency is not carrying a risk-on premium to give back. The offsetting tail is genuine: a live US-Iran conflict with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted is precisely the kind of event that produces a disorderly risk-off move, and in that scenario the krona's low liquidity means it sells off disproportionately. Two scheduled events inside the window - the 13 September Swedish election and the 16 September FOMC - could each shift the regime. On balance the risk environment is neither helping nor hurting the krona at the margin, and pretending otherwise would be an over-read of a broken correlation. Confidence is held to 53 rather than higher because the one official Swedish risk-appetite input, the Riksbank's Financial Markets Survey, was fielded between 30 March and 17 April 2026 and is roughly 137 days old at the valuation date, well outside the tactical freshness window.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the risk factor is a source of variance rather than of direction for the krona, and its weight halves to 0.05 accordingly. The structural point is that the krona's risk beta operates through the European industrial cycle rather than through commodity prices, which distinguishes it from the Norwegian krone and the Australian dollar. That channel is currently improving: the German manufacturing PMI reached 54.3 in its final August reading, above the 54.1 consensus, the strongest since May 2022 and a seventh consecutive month of expansion, and the ifo business climate index rose to 88.8 from 86.7. Germany takes roughly 10 per cent of Swedish goods exports and 72.9 per cent of Swedish exports go to European destinations, so a genuine German industrial recovery is the single most reliable external tailwind available to the krona. Against that stands the tail. A US-Iran conflict with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted is a live, unresolved situation, and the FocusEconomics panel explicitly says the split in its Riksbank forecasts hinges on how quickly the Hormuz crisis resolves. In a disorderly escalation the krona would be hit twice - once through the risk channel, where low liquidity amplifies the move, and once through the energy import bill - and no other currency in the G10 has that particular double exposure except the Norwegian krone in reverse. Sentiment indicators inside Sweden are constructive: household confidence has returned to normal, willingness to buy durables aside, and house-price expectations twelve months ahead rose to plus 4.2 per cent. The balance of a strengthening European industrial cycle against an unresolved energy-security tail is genuinely even, and a well-argued Neutral at 50 confidence is the honest reading rather than a forced direction.

tactical.analysis: Swedish krona positioning is structurally unobservable, and the honest response is a low-confidence Neutral rather than an invented number. CME lists a Swedish krona (SEK/USD) future and a EUR/SEK cross-rate future, but the krona is not a reportable line in the CFTC legacy Commitments of Traders financial futures report set that this pipeline consumes, because open interest sits far below the threshold that would generate a standalone series; the latest cached tranche of 11 August 2026 carries no krona line. CME lists no Swedish krona options at all - the exchange's own FX options trading codes table covers exactly seven pairs, AUD, GBP, CAD, EUR, JPY, CHF and CNH - so there is no exchange-based skew or options-implied positioning read either. This is a structural data absence rather than a retrieval failure, and any dossier quoting a CFTC net speculative position in the krona is quoting something that does not exist. What can be inferred comes from price and from the shape of the published forecast distribution. Four of the krona's nine crosses sit at or above the 96th percentile of their 52-week close distributions - EUR/SEK at 100, NOK/SEK at 100, AUD/SEK at 98 and SGD/SEK at 98 - which is the price signature of a persistently sold currency. Simultaneously the two corroborated numeric sell-side targets for end-2026, SEB at 10.45 and Bank of America at 10.50 for EUR/SEK, sit roughly six per cent through spot at 11.13. A market that is short a currency while publishing bullish targets on it has capitulated on timing but not on thesis, which is the configuration that produces sharp short-covering rallies on a catalyst. The Riksbank's own spring 2026 Financial Markets Survey adds that participants had reduced risk-taking and that krona liquidity, while good, had deteriorated slightly - thinner books amplify whatever flow does arrive. With no measurement and only inference, and with the Riksbank's Financial Markets Survey roughly 137 days old at the valuation date and therefore outside the tactical freshness window, 38 confidence is the appropriate ceiling.

tactical.what_is_priced: Price says the market is short the krona and has been rewarded for it; the published research says the same market expects the krona to rally six per cent by year-end. Both cannot be positioned for at once, so what is priced is a short position held with low conviction and a short leash. Our expectation is that the 24 September Monetary Policy Report is the most likely trigger for that leash to be pulled, and that the resulting move would be larger than the fundamental news warrants because the books are thin and one-sided.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the flow story that matters for the krona is structural rather than speculative, and it is durably negative. Sweden's institutional investor base is enormous relative to the size of its currency and is systematically short the krona through unhedged foreign assets. AP7, the default premium-pension fund, does not normally hedge its foreign currency exposure at all, and cited krona strength against the dollar as the main negative factor behind its 2025 return of 4.2 per cent, down from 27.3 per cent in 2024. The AP1 to AP4 buffer funds operate under a statutory limit on currency exposure that forces partial hedging, a requirement that an officially commissioned evaluation questioned after a year in which the hedge cost the funds gains from krona weakness. The economics of this are important: a stronger krona mechanically damages Swedish institutional returns, which creates a slow-moving hedging reaction function that leans against krona appreciation rather than a speculative one that reverses quickly. This is a large part of the answer to the chronic-weakness puzzle set out in the currency brief - a currency with a current account surplus, an AAA sovereign and among the lowest debt ratios in the G10 that nonetheless underperforms. On the other side, foreign demand for Swedish government bonds is being actively cultivated as issuance nearly doubles: the Debt Office raised SEK 20 billion in a new syndicated government bond and EUR 2 billion in a three-year foreign-currency bond during 2026, explicitly reaching investors not regularly active in the Swedish market, and nominal bond issuance rises from SEK 118 billion in 2025 to SEK 220 billion in 2026 and SEK 240 billion in 2027 with weekly auctions from 17 June. Heavier supply at higher yields is a genuine inbound portfolio channel that partly offsets the outbound pension channel. Neither dominates on a six-month view, and the foreign ownership share of Swedish government bonds could not be quantified from any dated 2026 source, so confidence stays low at 42.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Both horizons are Neutral and both carry unusually low confidence, for the same reason: there is no measurement. The tactical reading is inferential, drawn from close percentiles and a stale-bullish published forecast distribution; the strategic reading is structural, drawn from the mechanics of Swedish pension hedging and government bond supply. Strategic confidence is the higher of the two at 42 because structural flow facts are more durable than inferences from price percentiles, which can be invalidated by a single week's move. Neither is strong enough to contribute to a weighted score, and that is the correct outcome for a currency with no positioning data.
factors.contrarian_analysis_tactical: Positioning is stretched on every available proxy: four of nine krona crosses sit at or above the 96th percentile of their 52-week close distributions, EUR/SEK printed the highest Riksbank fixing of the trailing 52 weeks on 1 September, and NOK/SEK is within 20 pips of its high on a 60-pip average true range. For a currency with no measurable speculative position, close percentile at this extreme is the best available definition of stretched, and above roughly the 95th percentile is where reversal risk begins to dominate continuation. The unwind trigger is dated and specific: the 24 September Monetary Policy Report, where the Riksbank must revise up both 2026 growth and the assumed KIX and therefore its published rate path. A squeeze would be violent by krona standards precisely because there is no futures market to absorb it - all of the flow goes through a spot and forward market that the Riksbank's own survey describes as having deteriorated slightly in liquidity - and the historical analogue is the 2025 rally, in which the krona gained roughly 16.8 per cent against the dollar from a similarly cheap, similarly disliked starting point. The contrarian case is that a market short a currency while publishing six-per-cent-higher year-end targets on it is not positioned with conviction, and that the other side is seeing a central bank whose Governor has said in writing that the next move is a hike. Current positioning is therefore a mildly bullish signal for the krona - shorts to cover - rather than a neutral one, but the signal is too soft and too inferential to override the calendar sequencing that dominates the tactical window.
factors.contrarian_analysis_strategic: On a one-to-six-month view the contrarian case strengthens because the structural short becomes the constraint rather than the signal. The Swedish pension complex is short the krona by construction and cannot easily reverse, so a krona rally is not self-limiting through domestic profit-taking the way a speculative squeeze would be - it runs until the hedging reaction function catches up, which takes quarters rather than weeks. What would trigger it is the delivery of at least one Riksbank hike alongside a Norges Bank cut, which would compress the 250 basis point Scandinavian gap that has driven NOK/SEK to the 100th percentile. The severity assessment is asymmetric: the 2025 precedent of a roughly 16.8 per cent krona rally against the dollar shows what happens when a chronically cheap currency finally gets a catalyst in a thin market, and the absence of a futures market means there is no shock absorber. The genuine other side of the trade is that the same argument was available at the start of 2026 and has lost money all year, because the energy import bill and the passive Riksbank were the bigger facts. A contrarian who buys the krona on positioning alone, without the rates catalyst, is buying a currency whose trade surplus has collapsed by 83 per cent year to date - which is why this analysis informs the strategic Bullish call rather than driving it.

tactical.analysis: The external accounts are deteriorating fast and the mechanism is unambiguous: Sweden imports essentially all of its oil and gas, and both are in a supply shock. Brent settled at 94.65 dollars a barrel and WTI at 90.22 on 1 September 2026 as US-Iran hostilities escalated and the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted - a settlement carried by one source and contradicted by a second that quotes Brent at 91.28 dollars for the same date, a conflict flagged in the assumptions, while Dutch TTF gas reached about 70 euros a megawatt hour, with an intraday high of 70.49 euros on 31 August 2026, its highest since January 2023. The effect on the trade account is already visible and large. The July 2026 goods trade balance was a surplus of just SEK 1.2 billion against SEK 3.5 billion in July 2025, and the cumulative January-to-July surplus has collapsed to SEK 8.5 billion from SEK 51.4 billion a year earlier - an 83 per cent fall. Goods exports rose 4.0 per cent year on year in July while imports rose 6.0 per cent, so the surplus is being squeezed from the import side, which is exactly the signature of an energy price shock rather than an export demand problem. The current account is following: the latest published quarter, 2026-Q1, showed a surplus of SEK 94.0 billion, down SEK 37.4 billion year on year, with the goods surplus down SEK 14.1 billion and the services deficit widening to SEK 31.3 billion. Statistics Sweden's own framing is that the decline is largely driven by increased imports in the services balance and capital returns. The one clean Swedish export price in the set is also falling: North American NBSK pulp list prices declined 20 dollars a tonne in August to 1,770 dollars, with spot at 880 to 920 dollars net delivered. Base metals are the only offset - copper at 6.62 dollars a pound and aluminium at 3,278.15 dollars a tonne are both firm - but Sweden is a processor more than a miner, so high input metal prices are not an unambiguous positive. The tactical trigger is dated: Statistics Sweden publishes the second-quarter balance of payments on 4 September 2026, three days after the valuation date, and on the trajectory of the monthly goods data it is likely to show a further erosion.

strategic.analysis: At the strategic horizon this is the second heaviest factor in the framework at 0.16, and it is the principal drag on an otherwise krona-positive medium-term case. The structural position is still good in absolute terms - Statistics Sweden puts the first-quarter current account at 6.1 per cent of GDP, the cached point-in-time OECD vintage used in the macro comparison table for cross-currency consistency carries 4.5 per cent, and the NIER forecasts 4.7 per cent for 2026 and 4.3 per cent for 2027 - but the direction of travel is clearly negative and the driver is not cyclical. An energy shock transmits to a net importer through a permanent terms-of-trade loss for as long as it lasts, and this one is tied to a military conflict whose duration nobody can forecast. The offsetting force is real and is the strongest argument against this stance: the European industrial cycle, which is the demand side of Sweden's export book, is genuinely turning. German manufacturing PMI reached 54.3 in August, above the 54.1 consensus and the strongest since May 2022, with the recovery concentrated in inventory rebuilding, defence procurement and infrastructure investment - precisely the segments where Swedish engineering exporters sit. Germany takes about 10 per cent of Swedish goods exports and Europe as a whole 72.9 per cent, so the volume signal is improving even as the value signal deteriorates. That is exactly what an energy price shock does: it raises the import bill faster than recovering export volumes can offset it. Sweden's electricity mix, predominantly hydro and nuclear, limits the damage relative to continental peers, and defence exports at roughly 0.7 per cent of GDP in 2025 are a growing structural contributor as Sweden moves from 2.8 per cent of GDP defence spending in 2026 toward 3.5 per cent by 2030. Confidence is held to 52 rather than higher because the resolution of the Hormuz situation would flip this factor quickly, and because the second-quarter balance of payments due 4 September will immediately supersede the Q1 data underpinning it.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Both horizons are Bearish and the stance does not change; the confidence falls from 58 tactically to 52 strategically for two reasons. First, the tactical case rests on dated, published data - a July goods surplus of SEK 1.2 billion and an 83 per cent cumulative collapse - which are facts, whereas the strategic case requires a judgement on how long the energy shock persists. Second, the strategic horizon contains the offsetting German industrial recovery, which is accelerating and which the tactical window is too short to capture. The weight rises from 0.06 to 0.16, so the factor's contribution to the weighted score nearly triples even as confidence falls - which is the correct expression of a structural flow factor.

tactical.analysis: The Riksbank is the most transparent central bank in the G10 - it publishes its own projected policy-rate path and minutes that attribute views to named individuals - and what it published on 25 August is unambiguously hawkish relative to what the currency is pricing. The August meeting was a Monetary Policy Update containing no new forecasts, so the live official path is still June's, but the named minutes are richer than any forecast. Governor Erik Thedeen: I assess that our next change in the policy rate needs to be a raise, adding that last year's arguments in favour of a lower interest rate no longer apply and that the level of vigilance with regard to rising inflation must be high. Deputy Governor Anna Seim: my assessment is therefore that it may be necessary to raise the policy rate during the autumn. First Deputy Governor Aino Bunge argued the rate should be raised from somewhat stimulating to a more neutral level, while noting we are not there yet. Deputy Governor Goran Hjelm, dovish on the current level, described the risk outlook as still asymmetrical with the risk of inflation becoming too high being dominant, and warned that an escalation could entail much larger policy rate increases than the June path implies. Only Per Jansson is genuinely dovish, and even he hedged that if the bank fell behind the curve it could catch up with a few early rate increases in larger steps than the usual 0.25 percentage points. That is a four-to-one hawkish board with the dissenting dove pricing tail risk rather than denying it. Crucially for a currency dossier, the krona appears explicitly in the minutes: the Markets Department told the board that several analysts point out that a continued weakening of the krona, combined with the ECB being expected to continue raising its policy rate, could be a reason for the Riksbank to conduct a tighter monetary policy going forward. The immediate tactical qualifier is that the Riksbank has now signalled without acting for seven consecutive meetings, and BNY's Wee Khoon Chong argues it will hold off on being more assertive as long as measured inflation stays anchored - there is no Riksbank put under the krona at these levels.

That is a credibility discount applied to the most transparent central bank in the G10, and it is the cleanest mispricing in this dossier. Our expectation is that the 24 September Monetary Policy Report closes part of that discount by raising the published path, and that the currency reaction is larger than the bond reaction because the bond market has already moved 66.5 basis points at the front end while the currency has gone the other way.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months guidance carries a 0.12 weight, nearly double its tactical weight, and it is where the Riksbank's institutional design does most of its work. A published rate path and named minutes mean the market can track individual board members' positions over time, which makes Swedish forward guidance more informative than any anonymous-minutes central bank's. What that tracking currently shows is a board converging on tightening from different directions: Thedeen and Seim on activity and inflation risk, Bunge on the level relative to neutral, Hjelm on the asymmetry of the risk distribution. The Riksbank has an unusually good record of eventually doing what its path says, and its path says the end-point is approximately 2.2 per cent against a current 1.75 per cent. The exchange-rate channel makes the strategic case tighter still. The Riksbank is more willing than any other G10 central bank to state publicly that the krona matters for inflation, and its own June forecast assumed a KIX annual average of 116.18 against a spot of 120.20 - a 3.5 per cent miss on an import-weighted index in an economy where imported goods are a large share of the CPI basket. The September forecast round must mechanically raise imported inflation, and the drafting summary already records that the krona is somewhat weaker than at the June meeting. A further credibility marker sits outside the minutes: in its own 2026 reserve-allocation decision the Riksbank states that the analysis underlying the decision assumes a future appreciation of the Swedish krona, and hedges USD 8 billion and EUR 2 billion of reserves accordingly. That is an institution putting its balance sheet behind the view its communication implies. The risk to the strategic stance is the mirror image of its strength: because guidance is so explicit, a September path that is revised up by less than expected, or a Governor who softens the next-move-is-up language, would be a large and immediate negative.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Both horizons are Bullish, with strategic confidence marginally higher at 60 against 58, and the weight nearly doubles from 0.07 to 0.12. The reason confidence rises with horizon is that the Riksbank's guidance mechanism is a slow instrument: named minutes and a published path change market expectations over quarters, not weeks, and the seven-meeting gap between signalling and acting is a tactical liability but a strategic asset once the act finally arrives. The tactical horizon also carries the specific risk that the 24 September meeting produces words rather than a move, which would be read as an eighth consecutive failure to deliver even if the path is raised.

tactical.analysis: The tactical window contains the densest event calendar of the Swedish year, and the balance of those events is negative for the krona. The dominant item is the general election on Sunday 13 September 2026, confirmed by the Swedish Election Authority: all 349 Riksdag seats plus every regional and municipal council, with early voting open since 26 August and polls from 08:00 to 20:00. The result is genuinely uncertain and has been narrowing. Indikator Opinion had the centre-left opposition at 51.3 per cent against the governing bloc plus the Sweden Democrats at 46.6 per cent in late August, a 4.7 point gap against 8.9 points in June - the narrowest since autumn 2023 - and Demoskop on 24 August had 50.6 against 46.9, with the Social Democrats at 30.4 per cent, the Sweden Democrats at 18.3 and the Moderates at 17.2. With several small parties near the four per cent threshold, the seat arithmetic is more uncertain than the vote shares suggest. The second-order effect matters more than the result. Because 2026 is an election year, the Budget Bill for 2027 will not be presented in mid-September as it normally would; it follows the formation of a government, on a reported statutory backstop of no later than 12 November. That creates a two-month window in which the size of the post-election fiscal package is unknown, sitting directly on top of a widening deficit and an energy shock. Deputy Governor Seim named this explicitly in the August minutes: we are now facing opaque fiscal policy consequences of the general election in Sweden, as well as an American midterm election in November. Per Jansson added that fiscal policy is unusually expansionary and, in light of the election promises made recently, there is a risk that it may become even more expansionary. Layered on top is the live US-Iran conflict with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, which is both an energy shock and a risk-off tail for a low-liquidity currency.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the event set shifts from the election itself to what it produces, and the shape is still negative. The critical dated item is the Budget Bill for 2027, delayed from its usual September slot to roughly mid-November, which will reveal the size of the post-election fiscal package on top of a central government deficit already forecast at SEK 196 billion in 2026 and SEK 208 billion in 2027. The already-legislated 2026 election-year stance is expansionary - SEB put the reform package at approximately SEK 80 billion and the total expansionary effect at approximately SEK 130 billion including Ukraine support and defence - and SEB explicitly expects further unfunded reforms afterwards. The Riksbank's most dovish member has publicly flagged the risk that fiscal policy becomes even more expansionary. For a currency, an expansionary fiscal impulse into an economy already growing 3.3 per cent has an ambiguous first-order sign - it raises rates expectations as well as the deficit - but the second-order effect of pushing Maastricht debt to 39 per cent of GDP in 2027, at the edge of the 35 per cent debt anchor's tolerance band, is unambiguously negative for a currency whose entire premium rests on fiscal exceptionalism. The geopolitical layer is the second strategic driver. Sweden joined NATO in 2024 and is front-running the alliance timetable, moving from 2.8 per cent of GDP defence spending in 2026 toward 3.5 per cent by 2030 against NATO's 2035 target. That is a persistent fiscal commitment and a persistent export tailwind at the same time. The Middle East conflict is the dominant tail: a resolution would remove roughly half the bearish case in this dossier at a stroke, while an escalation that closed Hormuz for a sustained period would be the single worst outcome for a low-liquidity net energy importer. The US midterm elections on 3 November add a further layer of dollar-side variance inside the horizon.

tactical.analysis: On level, Sweden's fiscal position remains among the strongest in the developed world, and over a four-week horizon the level is what matters because nothing can change it. Maastricht general government debt was 35 per cent of GDP in 2025 and is forecast at 37 per cent in 2026, against ratios multiples of that across most of the G10, and the sovereign carries AAA from S&P Global Ratings, Aaa from Moody's and AAA from Morningstar DBRS, all on stable outlooks. Sweden operates one of the most disciplined fiscal frameworks anywhere - a surplus target over the cycle, an expenditure ceiling and a debt anchor of 35 per cent of GDP with a five percentage point tolerance band. There is no rating action pending, no auction stress, and no plausible path to a fiscal event inside four weeks: the Budget Bill has been pushed past the election to roughly mid-November, so the tactical window contains no fiscal document at all. The bond market corroborates. Sweden yields 202.6 basis points less than the United Kingdom and 159.6 basis points less than the United States at ten years despite vastly lower debt, which is the market pricing Swedish government bonds as a high-quality asset, and the Debt Office has been able to raise SEK 20 billion in a new syndicated government bond and EUR 2 billion in a three-year foreign-currency bond during 2026 while explicitly reaching investors not regularly active in the Swedish market. The move to weekly SEK 5 billion nominal auctions from 17 June has been absorbed without incident. The tactical stance is Bullish rather than Neutral because in an environment where an election is eleven days away and the fiscal trajectory is deteriorating, the fact that the starting point is AAA with 35 per cent debt is an active support for the currency rather than a neutral background. Confidence is capped at 52 because the direction of travel is clearly the wrong way and the market knows it.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the level and the trajectory pull in opposite directions with roughly equal force, which is what makes this a genuine Neutral rather than a diluted Bullish. The level remains exceptional: 37 per cent Maastricht debt in 2026, AAA across all three agencies, and one of the most disciplined fiscal frameworks in the world. The trajectory is the fastest deterioration in Sweden's recent history. The Debt Office's May 2026 forecast has the central government budget deficit widening to SEK 196 billion in 2026 and SEK 208 billion in 2027, nominal bond issuance rising from SEK 118 billion in 2025 to SEK 220 billion in 2026 and SEK 240 billion in 2027, and Maastricht debt reaching 39 per cent of GDP in 2027. The Debt Office states explicitly that this approaches the upper limit of the range for the debt anchor in Sweden's fiscal policy framework, although it remains low by international comparison. Director General Karolina Ekholm attributed the widening to increased defence spending, tax cuts, and new fiscal policy measures to mitigate the impact of the war in the Middle East. Three separate pressures compound over the horizon: a structural defence build toward 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2030, an unfunded post-election package that SEB expects and that the Riksbank's own dovish member has warned about, and a doubling of bond supply into a market where ten-year yields have already risen 35 basis points in a quarter. The offsetting argument is that a debt ratio moving from 35 to 39 per cent of GDP is a change in a number that remains, in absolute terms, better than almost any peer, and that higher yields on more supply are a genuine inbound portfolio attraction for a currency short of buyers. Neither side wins, and the honest score is Neutral at 52 confidence with a clearly identified trigger - the November Budget Bill - that would break the tie in either direction.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the structural picture flips from a clear negative to a genuinely balanced one, because the same levels that describe a downtrend also describe a range extreme. EUR/SEK has spent 53 weeks below a 200-week moving average at 11.22879 that is only 0.86 per cent above spot; on a six-month view the pair is therefore not trending into open space but pressing against the ceiling of a multi-year range whose floor at 10.50066 is 5.6 per cent below. The 2026 low of 10.50066 was set on 30 January and the high of 11.15276 in the last days of August, so the entire year has been a 6.2 per cent range with the currency now at the weak end of it. Sweden's chronic-weakness puzzle from the currency brief is the structural frame here: a currency with a current account surplus, an AAA sovereign, the lowest debt ratio but one in the G10 and a 37th-percentile real effective exchange rate that nonetheless trades at its 52-week weak extreme. The brief attributes this to a low-liquidity premium, small-open-economy vulnerability and housing-market risk perception, and the current configuration is a textbook instance rather than a new development. USD/SEK adds a different signal: it is 78 weeks below a falling 200-week average at 10.16904, so on the dollar cross the multi-year trend is krona-positive and spot at 9.57776 is in the upper part of a downtrend rather than at a fresh extreme, with a close percentile of 81 rather than 100. The volatility half of the factor is simply unavailable at any horizon, which caps confidence at 48 - one cannot assess whether a six-month view is cheap or expensive to express without a single implied volatility quote. factors.expression_assessment: The expression question cannot be answered properly, and saying so is more useful than pretending otherwise. CME lists no Swedish krona options, and no free dated quote for 1-month or 3-month EUR/SEK or USD/SEK implied volatility, the one-year implied percentile or the 25-delta risk reversal could be obtained, so it is impossible to say whether options are cheap or expensive, whether the variance risk premium is positive or negative, or whether the term structure carries an event premium into the 13 September election and the 24 September Monetary Policy Report. What can be said is that realised volatility is compressing into the densest event calendar of the Swedish year: EUR/SEK 20-day realised volatility of 4.30 per cent is below its 60-day reading of 4.66 per cent, and the fortnight from 10 to 24 September contains an ECB decision, a general election, a CPI print, an FOMC meeting with projections and a Riksbank Monetary Policy Report. In the absence of observable implied volatility, the defensible inference is that spot is the more reliable expression than options, simply because an option's value depends on a price one cannot see while spot's does not - and any option bought or sold into a dealer-quoted, non-transparent krona market carries an execution cost that cannot be benchmarked. On which cross: EUR/SEK is the cleaner instrument for a Sweden-specific view because it isolates Swedish against euro-area fundamentals and carries the lowest realised volatility in the set at 4.66 per cent over 60 days, so a given fundamental move produces a better signal-to-noise ratio; USD/SEK at 8.25 per cent 60-day realised volatility mostly expresses a dollar view. tactical.analysis: Dollar funding conditions are benign and are not currently a transmission channel into the krona, which is why this factor scores Neutral despite an 0.11 tactical weight. Secured overnight financing settled at 3.68 per cent on 31 August 2026 against interest on reserve balances of 3.65 per cent, a spread of just three basis points on a month-end date, with the 99th percentile print at 3.77 per cent only twelve basis points above IORB and volumes of 3.06 trillion dollars - the month's highest but not anomalous. The Federal Reserve's balance sheet stood at 6.731 trillion dollars on 26 August, down 14.8 billion on the week and essentially flat over twelve months following the end of quantitative tightening in December 2025, so no reserve-drain dynamic is operating. For Sweden specifically, the closest available proxy for a cross-currency basis is the BIS-sourced SEK/USD three-month forward premium published by the Riksbank, at minus 0.04825 krona on 1 September 2026. Against a spot of 9.58973 that annualises to minus 2.01 per cent, against a policy differential of minus 1.875 percentage points - a residual of roughly fourteen basis points, which is broadly covered-interest-parity consistent and shows no visible krona dollar-funding premium. The complicating tactical fact runs the other way. The broad dollar index fell 2.04 points to 118.7479 over the month, and the krona still lost 0.59 per cent against the dollar. A currency that cannot appreciate against a weakening dollar is telling you the marginal flow is not dollar-driven, and that removes the usual mechanism by which benign funding helps a small open-economy currency. Meanwhile the dollar side has turned hawkish at the margin: ten-year Treasury yields hit 4.81 per cent intraday on 1 September, the highest since November 2023, and the market is discussing Fed hike risk rather than cuts. Benign funding plus a firming dollar-rate impulse plus a broken transmission channel nets to zero, and that is the honest score.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the dollar cycle matters more for the krona than the dollar funding cycle, and the two point in different directions, which sustains a Neutral score at an 0.12 weight. On funding, the structural picture is as easy as it has been in years: quantitative tightening ended in December 2025, the Federal Reserve balance sheet is stable at 6.73 trillion dollars, the SOFR-IORB spread is three basis points, and there is no swap-line usage or reserve-scarcity dynamic in evidence. For a small open economy whose banks have moderate dollar funding needs through their Baltic and international operations, that is a genuine background positive and removes one of the three historical mechanisms by which the krona gets hurt. The dollar smile framework is the relevant strategic lens and it is unkind to the krona at both ends. Sweden's currency is highly vulnerable in a risk-off dollar squeeze because of low liquidity, and equally vulnerable in a US-exceptionalism regime because capital is drawn away from small European markets. The krona's best environment is the goldilocks middle - stable global growth, expanding European manufacturing and a broadly weakening dollar - and two of those three conditions are currently in place. The problem is that the third has stopped working: August delivered a 1.69 per cent broad dollar decline and expanding European manufacturing, and the krona weakened anyway. The strategic risk is that the Fed's next move is a hike rather than a cut, which would rebuild the dollar leg of the dollar smile and re-widen a 187.5 basis point differential that already costs a long-krona position roughly 2 per cent a year in the forwards. Set against that, a Fed that holds while the Riksbank hikes is the single cleanest path to a lower USD/SEK, and it is a plausible one. The honest reading is balance, with the qualifier that the cross-currency basis data needed to sharpen this factor are simply not available.

Its composition is the point. The largest weight in the framework, Policy and Rates at 0.24, contributes exactly zero because the euro-area hike lands fourteen days before the Swedish forecast round, and three further factors carrying a combined 0.31 weight - Risk Appetite, Flows and USD Liquidity - also contribute nothing. Conviction is 2 rather than 1 because the score is not merely small but genuinely two-sided - two factors argue strongly for the krona and three against, with dated catalysts on both sides inside the window - and 2 rather than 3 because the moving-average configuration on seven of nine krona crosses is against the currency, there is no positioning series with which to confirm the contrarian read, and a general election falls eleven days after the valuation date.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the framework is dominated by Policy and Rates at 0.24 and Inflation and Growth at 0.18, and those two account for 42 per cent of the score between them. The first contributes nothing and the second contributes almost everything positive, which is an unusual and informative configuration. Policy and Rates is Neutral not because the Swedish rate picture is ambiguous but because the calendar is: the European Central Bank meets on 10 September with more than 95 per cent priced for a hike to 2.50 per cent, widening the krona's euro deficit from 50 to 75 basis points, while the Riksbank does not publish a new path until 24 September. For fourteen of the next twenty-two trading days the differential moves against the krona on the schedule alone. Inflation and Growth is Bullish at 62 because the measured Swedish data are badly misleading: CPIF at 0.7 per cent in July is roughly 1.5 percentage points below the fiscally-adjusted 2.2 per cent that the Riksbank's own board members quote, while second-quarter GDP of plus 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter and plus 3.3 per cent year on year beat the central bank's full-year forecast in a single quarter. These two factors interact rather than merely coexist: the growth and inflation surprise is precisely what will force the 24 September path revision, so the positive factor is the mechanism by which the zero-scoring factor eventually turns positive - just not inside four weeks. Working against them, External Balance at minus 0.0348, Event Risk at minus 0.0300 and Market Structure at minus 0.0275 form a coherent bear bloc: an 83 per cent collapse in the January-to-July goods surplus to SEK 8.5 billion driven by a 94.65 dollar Brent settlement and 70 euro TTF gas, a general election on 13 September with the bloc gap halved since June, and EUR/SEK at the 100th percentile of its 52-week close distribution with moving averages stacked against the krona. What is priced is a Riksbank that talks and does not act - seven consecutive holds have earned it a credibility discount - and just over one 25 basis point hike by end-2026. strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework redistributes toward structure: Policy and Rates holds its 0.24 but External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16, Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12 and USD Liquidity from 0.11 to 0.12, while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Risk Appetite from 0.10 to 0.05. That reweighting is what turns a Neutral tactical score into a Bullish strategic one, because it promotes the two factors on which the Swedish case is strongest - the direction of the policy rate and the credibility of the guidance behind it - while demoting the near-term calendar noise. The core claim is simple and quantifiable. Sweden runs a 1.75 per cent policy rate against an economy growing 3.3 per cent year on year, with underlying inflation that the central bank itself puts at approximately 2.2 per cent once its own temporary tax measures are stripped out, giving a negative real policy rate of about minus 0.45 percentage points. Its Governor has stated in writing that the next change in the policy rate needs to be a rise, a second board member says it may be necessary during the autumn, a third argues the rate should move toward neutral, and the fourth describes the risk distribution as asymmetrically tilted toward inflation being too high. The June path already carries an end-point of approximately 2.2 per cent. Meanwhile the peers that out-yield the krona are at or past their peaks: Norges Bank at 4.25 per cent has room to cut, the RBNZ's easing bias is exhausted, the Bank of Canada is finished and the Bank of England has an easing bias, so the krona's disadvantage narrows against four of the seven currencies that currently out-yield it. These two factors reinforce each other - the guidance is credible precisely because the published path is a formal forecast rather than rhetoric - while the conflict is with External Balance, where an 83 per cent collapse in the year-to-date goods surplus to SEK 8.5 billion is a real, measured, ongoing drain that a rate differential cannot offset. What is priced is roughly one 25 basis point hike by end-2026 against the NIER's forecast of one this year and another in 2027, so the market carries perhaps 25 to 40 basis points less tightening than the domestic forecast community; what is priced in the currency is even less, since EUR/SEK made a 52-week high while Swedish two-year yields rose 66.5 basis points over twelve months. That divergence - the bond market repricing hawkishly while the currency weakens - is the central edge in this dossier. The path of least resistance over six months is a grinding krona recovery toward the 10.8494 to 10.95998 support band on EUR/SEK, punctuated by the November Budget Bill. The key dated catalysts are the Riksbank on 24 September, 4 November and 16 December, the Budget Bill by roughly 12 November, and the ECB on 10 September, 29 October and 17 December. Actionability is moderate: EUR/SEK offers the cleanest expression at 4.66 per cent 60-day realised volatility with a defined invalidation at the 200-week average, but the absence of any krona options market means the view can only be held in spot or forwards, and the forward costs about 70 basis points a year against the euro.

consensus_divergence.our_view: We are less bullish than the surviving sell-side targets and more bullish than the market. Our six-month base case is EUR/SEK 10.80, roughly 3.3 per cent above the SEB and Bank of America targets and about 2.9 per cent below spot, on a Riksbank that hikes once by December and signals a second move for 2027. We are also explicitly Neutral tactically, which the January-vintage bullish targets are not, because the September calendar front-loads the euro-positive event and back-loads the krona-positive one.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: We differ from the sell-side because their targets predate both the energy shock and the collapse of the goods trade surplus from SEK 51.4 billion to SEK 8.5 billion year to date, and because a 10.45 target implies the krona recovers its entire 2026 loss in four months on a currency whose central bank has held seven consecutive times. We differ from the market in the opposite direction because the market is anchoring on measured CPIF of 0.7 per cent rather than the fiscally-adjusted 2.2 per cent that the Riksbank's own board quotes, and is therefore under-weighting a September forecast round that must absorb a second-quarter GDP print exceeding the full-year forecast and a KIX index 3.5 per cent weaker than assumed. The market is also ignoring the divergence between the Swedish bond market, where two-year yields have risen 66.5 basis points over twelve months and the ten-year is at its highest since October 2023, and the currency, which made a 52-week low over the same period. In short, the sell-side is right about direction and wrong about magnitude and timing; the market is right about timing and wrong about the inflation measure it is watching.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: The three-month outright is built on a real quoted number - the BIS forward premium of minus 0.04825 krona published through the Riksbank for 1 September 2026 - which annualises to minus 2.01 per cent against a policy differential of minus 1.875 percentage points, a residual of roughly fourteen basis points. The important structural point is that the forwards contain no view: they say only that the dollar out-yields the krona by roughly two per cent, which is the textbook no-arbitrage outcome. All of the tradeable content is in the gap between the forward and our expectation, and that gap is negligible at one month and large at three and six - which is the cleanest single statement of why this dossier is Neutral tactically and Bullish strategically.
