key_catalysts.rationale: The first quarterly current account since the energy shock intensified, and the release that will supersede the 2026-Q1 surplus of SEK 94.0 billion used throughout this dossier. On the trajectory of the monthly goods data - a January-to-July surplus of SEK 8.5 billion against SEK 51.4 billion a year earlier - a further year-on-year deterioration is close to certain.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the market has seen the July goods figure of plus SEK 1.2 billion but not the quarterly current account that contains it.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and USD/SEK; the external balance is the heaviest strategic counterweight in this dossier at a 0.16 weight.

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden CPI flash estimate, August 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The flash lands a week before the full release and gives the first read on whether the summer's upside inflation momentum continued. Danske forecasts CPIF at 1.00 per cent and CPIF excluding energy at 0.74 per cent, both above July's 0.7 and 0.6 per cent. A beat would begin the repricing this dossier expects; a miss would undermine its central analytical claim.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - Danske's forecast is public but the market is anchored on the low measured level rather than the fiscally-adjusted rate.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK most directly, since it isolates the Swedish-versus-euro-area inflation comparison.

key_catalysts.event: European Central Bank Governing Council decision with staff projections
key_catalysts.rationale: More than 95 per cent priced for a 25 basis point hike to 2.50 per cent on ECB board member Nagel's own characterisation, with euro-area August inflation at 3.3 per cent, the highest since September 2023. The move mechanically widens the krona's euro deficit from 50 to 75 basis points and takes the EUR/SEK carry-to-volatility ratio from minus 0.107 to about minus 0.161. Because it is fully priced, the risk is in the projections and the guidance rather than the decision.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced as to the decision; the December path is roughly evenly split between 2.50 and 2.75 per cent.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK above all; this is the single most consequential scheduled event for the krona inside the tactical window.

key_catalysts.event: Swedish general election - all 349 Riksdag seats plus regional and municipal councils
key_catalysts.rationale: Confirmed by the Swedish Election Authority, with early voting open since 26 August and polls from 08:00 to 20:00. The bloc gap has halved since June, to 4.7 points on Indikator Opinion and 3.7 on Demoskop, the narrowest since autumn 2023, and several small parties sit near the four per cent threshold, so the seat arithmetic is more uncertain than the vote shares. The market impact runs through the fiscal channel rather than the policy channel, since the Riksbank's mandate is unaffected.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - no retrievable sell-side analysis quantifies a Swedish election risk premium in EUR/SEK, which is itself the notable fact.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and NOK/SEK; a protracted coalition negotiation would extend the fiscal information vacuum to mid-November or beyond.

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden CPI, CPIF and CPIF excluding energy, August 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The most important Swedish data point before the Riksbank meets. July printed CPIF at 0.7 per cent and CPIF excluding energy at 0.6 per cent, against fiscally-adjusted equivalents of approximately 2.2 and 1.6 per cent. A CPIF print at or above Danske's 1.00 per cent forecast makes the September path revision straightforward; a miss makes it discretionary and would materially weaken this dossier's central claim.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a modest rise is expected but the market is not positioned for the underlying rate being at target.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; also NOK/SEK, since Norwegian CPI-ATE at 2.7 per cent is the comparison that drives the Scandinavian differential.

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The Fed is expected to hold at 3.50 to 3.75 per cent, but the risk is asymmetric toward a hawkish surprise: three regional presidents dissented in favour of a hike on 29 July 2026, and ten-year Treasury yields reached 4.81 per cent intraday on 1 September, the highest since November 2023. A hawkish dot plot would widen the krona's 187.5 basis point dollar disadvantage and firm the broad dollar.
key_catalysts.priced_in: A hold is fully priced; the distribution of the projections is not.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/SEK primarily; the krona is currently failing to benefit from dollar weakness, so a firmer dollar would compound rather than offset.

key_catalysts.event: Swedish Labour Force Survey and Public Employment Service unemployment, August 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: Two different Swedish unemployment series report in the same week and they tell opposite stories: the Labour Force Survey seasonally adjusted trend at 8.7 per cent in July is the highest in the G10, while registered unemployment at 6.5 per cent and the register-based BAS measure at 5.1 per cent have both been falling for months. The Riksbank has repeatedly cited labour-market slack as the reason not to hike, so the survey measure carries disproportionate policy weight.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as a policy input; the market treats Swedish unemployment as structurally high and stable.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; a further rise in the survey trend rate would be the most credible reason for the Riksbank to soften its September guidance.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank policy rate decision and Monetary Policy Report with a new published rate path
key_catalysts.rationale: The single most important dated event in this dossier and the inflection point between the two horizons. It is the first full forecast round since June and must incorporate second-quarter GDP of plus 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter against a 2.2 per cent full-year forecast, and a KIX at 120.20 against an assumed 116.18 - both of which push the published path up. Governor Thedeen has said the next change must be a rise; Seim has flagged the autumn.
key_catalysts.priced_in: A hold is fully priced. Just over one 25 basis point hike is priced by end-2026, so a path revision of 20 basis points or more at the end-2026 point would be a genuine hawkish surprise.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All krona crosses, but EUR/SEK and NOK/SEK most of all - the latter because Norges Bank publishes its own Monetary Policy Report the same day.

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden register-based labour market status (BAS), August 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The register-based measure has fallen for six to seven consecutive months to 5.1 per cent in June, against a survey trend rate of 8.7 per cent, and the employment rate for ages 20 to 64 has risen to 81.8 per cent. If the Riksbank begins citing this series rather than the Labour Force Survey, the principal dovish argument on the board weakens considerably.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the series is not widely followed outside Sweden.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; relevant mainly as a slow-burning input to the Riksbank's reaction function.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank minutes of the 24 September monetary policy meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: Swedish minutes attribute views to named individuals, so this release shows whether the hawkish majority hardened or softened after seeing the September forecast round. The specific thing to look for is whether Jansson, the sole dove, moves, and whether Hjelm shifts from dovish-on-the-level to hawkish-on-the-level.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - minutes are typically a second-order event but Swedish named minutes carry more information than most.

key_catalysts.event: European Central Bank Governing Council decision
key_catalysts.rationale: If the ECB delivers in September and signals a further move, this is the meeting at which the euro-area rate could reach 2.75 per cent, taking the krona's euro disadvantage to 100 basis points. Euro-area inflation at 3.3 per cent and rising for a second month makes a follow-up move credible.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Roughly evenly split between a hold and a further hike by December.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; the differential path against the euro is the main structural risk to the strategic bullish krona case.

key_catalysts.rationale: Named explicitly by Deputy Governor Seim in the August minutes as a source of uncertainty alongside the Swedish election. The transmission to the krona is entirely indirect, through the dollar and through global risk appetite, but for a low-liquidity currency an event that moves the broad dollar moves USD/SEK disproportionately.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced in krona terms at all.

key_catalysts.rationale: An interim meeting with no new forecasts, which makes it the most plausible date for an actual hike if the September path is raised and the October data cooperate. Anna Seim has said it may be necessary to raise during the autumn, and this is the last meeting that qualifies as autumn.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Largely unpriced as a live meeting; the market's roughly one hike by end-2026 is more naturally attributed to December.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All krona crosses; a hike here rather than in December would be the clearest possible refutation of the credibility discount.

key_catalysts.event: Budget Bill for 2027 presented to the Riksdag
key_catalysts.rationale: Delayed from its usual mid-September slot because 2026 is an election year, on a reported statutory backstop of no later than 12 November. It will reveal the size of the post-election unfunded package on top of a central government deficit forecast at SEK 208 billion for 2027 and a Maastricht debt ratio heading to 39 per cent of GDP, at the edge of the debt anchor's tolerance band. SEB expects new unfunded reforms aimed mainly at households.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the market treats Swedish fiscal policy as a non-issue, which has been correct for a decade.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and the Swedish government bond curve; a package materially above the SEK 80 billion 2026 precedent would be the first genuinely negative Swedish fiscal event in years.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank policy rate decision and Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The final scheduled opportunity for the Riksbank to deliver the hike its June path implied for 2026, and the meeting the market most naturally associates with the roughly one hike it prices. A failure to move here, with a full forecast round in hand, would be the eighth consecutive hold and would validate the credibility discount for another year.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - this is the meeting that carries most of the roughly one 25 basis point hike priced by end-2026.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All krona crosses; also NOK/SEK, since Norges Bank publishes its own Monetary Policy Report the following day.

key_catalysts.event: European Central Bank Governing Council decision with staff projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The euro-area end-point for 2026. If the ECB reaches 2.75 per cent while the Riksbank remains at 1.75 per cent, the krona's euro disadvantage is 100 basis points against 50 at the valuation date, and the strategic bullish case would need the Swedish hike to arrive in the first quarter of 2027 instead.

invalidators.condition: EUR/SEK records a weekly close above the 200-week moving average at 11.22879
invalidators.mechanism: The 200-week average has capped EUR/SEK for 53 consecutive weeks and defines the top of the multi-year range on which the entire strategic case rests. A weekly close above it converts a range top into a breakout, invites systematic trend capital that is already short the krona to add, and removes the structural argument that the downside is bounded.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EUR/SEK weekly close against the 200-week simple moving average

invalidators.condition: The 24 September Monetary Policy Report leaves the published rate path unchanged or lower at the end-2026 point
invalidators.mechanism: The strategic bullish case rests almost entirely on the Riksbank validating its own guidance. A path that is not raised despite a second-quarter GDP print exceeding the full-year forecast and a KIX 3.5 per cent weaker than assumed would mean the bank is deliberately looking through both, which would confirm the market's credibility discount and remove the plus 0.1392 Policy and Rates contribution from the strategic score.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Riksbank published policy-rate path, end-2026 and end-2027 points, against the June 2026 path
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Quarterly, at each Monetary Policy Report
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: End-2026 path point unchanged at or below the June level, or explicit removal of the phrase that the probability of a rise remains

invalidators.condition: August or September CPIF prints below 0.6 per cent year on year
invalidators.mechanism: The central analytical claim of this dossier is that measured CPIF understates the underlying rate by about 1.5 percentage points and is turning up. A print below the July level would mean the fiscal drag is larger or more persistent than the Riksbank's own estimate, would push measured inflation further below target, and would give the board's dovish wing the evidence it currently lacks.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Statistics Sweden CPIF, year on year
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: CPIF below 0.6 per cent year on year in either the August or September reference month

invalidators.condition: Brent crude sustains above 105 dollars a barrel for a month, or Dutch TTF gas above 85 euros a megawatt hour
invalidators.mechanism: Sweden imports essentially all of its oil and gas. At current prices the January-to-July goods surplus has already collapsed 83 per cent to SEK 8.5 billion; a further leg higher would push the monthly goods balance into deficit and take the current account below four per cent of GDP, turning the heaviest strategic counterweight from a drag into the dominant factor.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Brent front-month settlement and Dutch TTF front-month
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Brent above 105 dollars or TTF above 85 euros per megawatt hour on a 20-day average

invalidators.condition: The Swedish general election produces a hung parliament that is unresolved four weeks after 13 September
invalidators.mechanism: The Budget Bill for 2027 follows the formation of a government. A protracted coalition negotiation extends the fiscal information vacuum past the reported mid-November backstop into a period when the Debt Office is issuing SEK 220 billion of nominal bonds at weekly auctions, and would add a political risk premium to a currency that is already at a 52-week weak extreme.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Riksdag speaker's mandate process and government formation news flow
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: No prime minister elected by 11 October 2026

invalidators.condition: The European Central Bank reaches 2.75 per cent by December while the Riksbank remains at 1.75 per cent
invalidators.mechanism: That combination takes the krona's euro policy disadvantage to 100 basis points from 50 at the valuation date and takes the EUR/SEK carry-to-volatility ratio from minus 0.107 to about minus 0.215. It would also mean the Riksbank had passed on three consecutive opportunities to act after signalling, which is a credibility event rather than a rates event.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB deposit rate against the Riksbank policy rate
invalidators.monitor_frequency: At each ECB and Riksbank meeting
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Euro-area rate at 2.75 per cent and Swedish rate at 1.75 per cent on 18 December 2026

invalidators.condition: The 2027 Budget Bill contains an unfunded package materially above the SEK 80 billion 2026 precedent, or a rating agency places Sweden on negative outlook
invalidators.mechanism: Sweden's currency premium rests on fiscal exceptionalism. The Debt Office already projects Maastricht debt at 39 per cent of GDP in 2027, which it says approaches the upper limit of the debt anchor's range. A larger package or a rating action would remove the one unambiguously positive structural feature of the Swedish story.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Budget Bill reform total and rating agency releases
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Unfunded reforms above SEK 100 billion, or any AAA outlook change

factors_changed.reason: The August minutes replaced inference with an explicit statement: the Governor now says the next change in the policy rate needs to be a rise, and market pricing has moved to just over one hike by end-2026. The level of Swedish carry is unchanged and still deeply negative, but its direction is no longer ambiguous, which lifts the tactical stance out of Bearish without making it Bullish given the 10 September ECB hike.

Three things changed together: the board is now demonstrably four-to-one hawkish on named minutes, the Swedish ten-year has risen 35 basis points in a quarter to its highest since October 2023, and second-quarter GDP beat the Riksbank's full-year forecast in one quarter. The strategic differential now narrows against four of the seven peers that out-yield the krona.

The 28 August national accounts printed plus 1.6 per cent quarter on quarter and plus 3.3 per cent year on year, the manufacturing PMI reached 56.1 and household confidence returned to normal for the first time since November 2024. The quantified size of the temporary fiscal drag - about 1.5 percentage points, taking July CPIF from a measured 0.7 to an adjusted 2.2 per cent - was also established from the Riksbank's own board members rather than inferred.

factors_changed.factor: 5: External Balance & Terms of Trade - tactical
factors_changed.reason: Confidence rose because the damage is now measured rather than anticipated: the cumulative January-to-July goods surplus has collapsed to SEK 8.5 billion from SEK 51.4 billion a year earlier, and Brent settled at 94.65 dollars with TTF gas at its highest since January 2023.

factors_changed.factor: 5: External Balance & Terms of Trade - strategic
factors_changed.reason: The energy shock has persisted long enough to be treated as a structural rather than a transitory drag on a 0.16-weighted factor, and the first-quarter current account has confirmed a SEK 37.4 billion year-on-year deterioration.

The 25 August publication of named minutes containing the Governor's statement that the next change must be a rise, plus the Markets Department's explicit link between a weakening krona and tighter policy, converted guidance from ambiguous to directional.

The general election is now eleven days away rather than six weeks, the bloc gap has halved since June to 3.7 to 4.7 points, and it has been established that the 2027 Budget Bill will not appear until roughly mid-November, creating a two-month fiscal information vacuum.

The Debt Office's forecast of a SEK 208 billion deficit in 2027, bond issuance rising to SEK 240 billion and Maastricht debt reaching 39 per cent of GDP - which it says approaches the upper limit of the debt anchor's range - now offsets the exceptional starting level over a strategic horizon.

EUR/SEK has moved from 10.9783 to 11.12656 and is now pressing a 200-week average at 11.22879 that has capped it for 53 weeks. On a six-month view the same price that reads as a downtrend now also reads as a range extreme with a defined ceiling, which is genuinely balanced rather than negative.

The krona-risk correlation broke down during August: the VIX fell 6.23 points and the broad dollar fell 2.04 points while the KIX rose 1.12 per cent. A supportive risk backdrop that the currency demonstrably does not capture cannot be scored as a positive.

conviction_change.explanation: Conviction is unchanged at 2 on both horizons, but the stances beneath it moved in opposite directions. Tactically the krona improved from Bearish at minus 0.1606 to Neutral at plus 0.0807, a 24 point swing in the weighted score driven almost entirely by the Policy and Rates factor moving from Bearish to Neutral and Inflation and Growth from Neutral to Bullish. Strategically the stance stayed Bullish but the score rose from plus 0.1195 to plus 0.1605 as Policy and Rates moved from Neutral to Bullish and Guidance strengthened, partly offset by External Balance turning Bearish and Fiscal turning Neutral. The G10 rank improved from 9 to 6 tactically and from 5 to 3 strategically.

new_catalysts: The Swedish general election of 13 September 2026 has entered the tactical window, confirmed by the Swedish Election Authority, with early voting open since 26 August and the bloc gap halved since June

It has been established that the Budget Bill for 2027 will not be presented in September because it is an election year, on a reported statutory backstop of no later than 12 November - creating a two-month fiscal information vacuum that did not feature in the previous dossier

The European Central Bank meeting of 10 September is now more than 95 per cent priced for a hike, against a materially less certain expectation a month ago, and euro-area August inflation reached 3.3 per cent, the highest since September 2023

The 24 September Riksbank Monetary Policy Report has become the identified inflection point between the two horizons, because it is the first forecast round to incorporate the 28 August GDP release and a KIX 3.5 per cent weaker than assumed

seasonality.pattern: Swedish year-end portfolio rebalancing by the AP buffer funds and the wider domestic pension complex, which holds large unhedged foreign asset books, plus the general G10 pattern of thinner year-end liquidity in low-turnover currencies.
seasonality.relevance_window: Late November to early January, which falls inside the strategic one-to-six-month horizon but outside the tactical two-to-four-week window.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified. No documented, measurable Swedish krona seasonal effect of the kind that exists for the yen's March and September fiscal-year-end repatriation could be sourced, and the pattern is asserted here only as a liquidity characteristic rather than a directional edge.
seasonality.current_alignment: Neutral and explicitly not relied upon. The one genuine calendar feature worth noting is not seasonal but structural: the 2026 electoral cycle has pushed the Budget Bill from its normal September slot to roughly mid-November, so the usual autumn fiscal information flow is displaced by about two months this year.

assumptions: Provenance convention. Figures drawn from the pipeline data cache are dated in the text with their as-of date and recorded here rather than in the numbered citation list, per pipeline convention. The cache supplies: spot rates, moving averages including the 200-week, ATR, 20-day and 60-day realised volatility, support and resistance zones and 52-week range and close percentiles for every cross; all ten G10 policy rates; the point-in-time OECD and Eurostat macro dashboard; BIS real effective exchange rates; the authoritative central-bank meeting calendar and the economic event calendar; and the US curve, risk and commodity block - DGS2, DGS5, DGS10, DGS30, T10Y2Y, T10Y3M, T10YIE, T5YIE, DFII10, VIXCLS, BAMLC0A0CM, BAMLH0A0HYM2, DCOILBRENTEU, DCOILWTICO, DHHNGSP and the broad dollar index DTWEXBGS. Everything sourced from the web carries a numbered citation, with the exceptions listed in the research-sourced register below.

DOCUMENTED GAP - implied volatility, risk reversals and volatility term structure. CME lists Swedish krona futures (SEK/USD and EUR/SEK cross-rate) but lists NO Swedish krona options: the exchange's own FX options trading codes table covers only AUD, GBP, CAD, EUR, JPY, CHF and CNH. No free dated quote for 1-month or 3-month EUR/SEK or USD/SEK implied volatility, the 1-year implied percentile, the 25-delta risk reversal or the volatility term structure could be obtained from any venue. The iv_1m, iv_3m and iv_percentile_1y fields in the JSON are ZERO PLACEHOLDERS and must not be read as market levels, and the vol_term_structure value of Flat is a schema default rather than an observation.

DOCUMENTED GAP - CFTC positioning. The Swedish krona is not a reportable line in the CFTC legacy Commitments of Traders financial futures report set that this pipeline consumes; the latest cached tranche of 2026-08-11 carries no krona line. This is a structural data absence rather than a retrieval failure, and all positioning fields in the JSON are structural placeholders. Positioning is inferred from 52-week close percentiles, from the published forecast distribution and from the structure of Swedish institutional FX hedging.

DOCUMENTED GAP - cross-currency basis. No quoted Swedish krona cross-currency basis and no dated end-August 3-month EUR/USD or USD/JPY basis benchmark was obtainable. The EUR/USD figure of approximately minus 16 to minus 20 basis points is dated mid-May 2026, roughly 3.5 months before the valuation date, from a commercial glossary page, and is flagged as stale. The BIS-sourced SEK/USD 3-month forward premium published through the Riksbank is used as the closest available proxy.

DOCUMENTED GAP - purchasing power parity. No free purchasing-power-parity source was obtainable. The PPP deviation table is a REER-RELATIVE PROXY computed as Sweden's BIS real effective exchange rate of 96.46 divided by each peer's, minus one, and applied to the pipeline spot rate. It is labelled as such in every row and is not a purchasing-power-parity fair value. The NZD row cannot be expressed as a rate at all, because the vendor carries no NZD/SEK series.

DOCUMENTED GAP - forward points at 1 month and 6 months. Only the 3-month tenor is a real quoted number: the BIS-sourced SEK/USD 3-month forward premium of minus 0.04825 krona for 1 September 2026, published through the Riksbank. The 1-month and 6-month outrights of 9.56170 and 9.48138 are DERIVED at the same annualised minus 2.01 per cent rate. The Riksbank publishes a 6-month series (SEKUSDFO6MFIX) but it returned no data on repeated requests, and no EUR/SEK forward series exists in the SWEA catalogue; the EUR/SEK forward outrights are derived from the cached futures-implied roll premium of minus 69.7 basis points annualised.

DOCUMENTED GAP - Swedish 2-year yield source. The Swedish 2-year of 2.53 per cent as at 31 August 2026 comes from a single secondary source. The Riksbank publishes a 2-year generic series (SEGVB2YC) but it returned no data on repeated requests, so unlike the 10-year - which is corroborated by the Riksbank's own series at 3.134 per cent against the secondary source's 3.14 per cent - the 2-year and therefore the 2s10s curve figure of plus 60 basis points are single-sourced and flagged.

DOCUMENTED GAP - foreign ownership of Swedish government bonds. The Debt Office hosts a foreign-holdings series but no dated 2026 percentage could be extracted, so the inbound portfolio channel in Factor 4 is described qualitatively rather than quantified.

DOCUMENTED GAP - household debt ratios. No 2026-dated aggregate Swedish household debt-to-disposable-income or debt-to-GDP ratio was obtainable. The Financial Stability Report 2026:1 states only that the ratio has continued to decline and is now at the same level as ten years ago. A precise figure is deliberately not quoted; the mortgage-specific facts used instead - SEK 4,334 billion outstanding, 77 per cent at variable rates, a new variable rate of 2.74 per cent and household lending growth of 3.3 per cent year on year - are all sourced from Statistics Sweden for July 2026.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - sovereign ratings. AAA from S&P Global Ratings, Aaa from Moody's and AAA from Morningstar DBRS, all stable, could not be confirmed with a 2026-dated agency page because rating-agency sites are JavaScript-rendered and return no fetchable dated content. The rating picture is best available rather than verified.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - the 2027 Budget Bill date. The election-year delay past September is reliable, but the specific statutory backstop of no later than 12 November 2026 comes from a search-result summary of Swedish government material and could not be verified verbatim on a fetched primary page. The catalyst is dated 2026-11-W2 rather than to a specific day for that reason.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - election polling. Bloc standings of 51.3 against 46.6 per cent (Indikator Opinion, late August) and 50.6 against 46.9 per cent (Demoskop, 24 August) and the party shares of Social Democrats 30.4, Sweden Democrats 18.3 and Moderates 17.2 per cent come from secondary reporting of those polls rather than from the pollsters' own pages. The election date itself is confirmed from the Swedish Election Authority's own site.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - bank forecasts. Only two named EUR/SEK targets could be individually corroborated: SEB at 10.45 for December 2026 from its own site, and Bank of America at 10.50 for year-end 2026 from a full retrieved article. Both are January 2026 vintage and therefore roughly seven months stale. Attributions circulating for ING at 10.30 and Danske at 11.00 could NOT be corroborated - the ING page returns an empty body and the Danske figure appears only on a forecast aggregator - and are deliberately excluded from the consensus section rather than reported.

CONTESTED FIGURE, RESOLVED - July CPIF. One secondary source reports Swedish CPIF at 3.0 per cent year on year for July 2026. That figure is rejected: Statistics Sweden's own release for the July reference month, published 13 August 2026, gives CPIF at 0.7 per cent, and the Riksbank's own board members quote 0.7 per cent measured against approximately 2.2 per cent adjusted for temporary fiscal measures. Statistics Sweden's published twelve-month table shows CPIF at 3.0 per cent in July 2025, which is the most likely origin of the error. This dossier uses 0.7 per cent measured and approximately 2.2 per cent adjusted throughout, and a separately circulating claim of August CPIF above 3 per cent from an unretrievable preview is likewise excluded.

STALE - cached sovereign 10-year series. The cached IRLTLT01 sovereign 10-year series are MONTHLY and as at 2026-06-01, roughly 92 days old, breaching both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows. The Swedish leg has been REPLACED for this dossier with the Riksbank's own published series at 3.134 per cent for 1 September 2026 against the cached 2.781 per cent, a difference of 35.3 basis points. The German, US, UK, Japanese and Norwegian legs used in the key spreads are matched 31 August 2026 closes carried consistently across this cycle; the Swiss, Canadian and Australian legs remain the cached monthly values and are flagged as stale in their own interpretations.

STALE - other cached series. The BIS REER period is 2026-06, roughly 63 days before the valuation date and marginally outside the strategic freshness window. The cached CFTC tranche of 2026-08-11 carries no krona line and is not used for any figure. The cached AUD and NOK policy rates carry an as-of date of 2026-07-01 rather than late August, though neither central bank has moved. Cached Brent of 88.24 dollars for 25 August is superseded in the text by the 94.65 dollar settlement of 1 September and both are given.

Methodological choice - carry-to-volatility denominator. Every carry-to-volatility ratio is stated as annualised carry in percentage points divided by 60-day REALISED volatility read directly from the cached derived file for each cross, never estimated, never recomputed and never constructed from two dollar legs. No implied-volatility-based ratio is given because no implied volatility exists for any krona cross.

Methodological choice - primary pair and conventions. USD/SEK is treated as the primary reference pair per the currency brief, but EUR/SEK is used for market structure, key levels and the cleanest expression of a Sweden-specific view, because it isolates Swedish against euro-area fundamentals, carries the lowest realised volatility in the set and is the Riksbank's own focus. Both quotes are inverted for the base currency and this is stated wherever a direction is given.

Methodological choice - price anchor. Spot rates, moving averages, zones and percentiles come from the pipeline price store at the 31 August 2026 close, for cross-currency consistency with the other ten dossiers in this cycle. The Riksbank's own official fixings for the same date - USD/SEK 9.58089 and EUR/SEK 11.1100 - differ by roughly 3 and 165 pips respectively because of the fixing time, and both are reported wherever the difference could matter.

Methodological choice - central bank dates. All central-bank decision dates come from the pipeline's authoritative calendar file and were never web-searched. Singapore has no policy rate by design; the Monetary Authority of Singapore operates an exchange-rate band reviewed semi-annually.

Interpretive choice - which inflation rate is the analytical anchor. This dossier treats the fiscally-adjusted CPIF of approximately 2.2 per cent, not the measured 0.7 per cent, as the rate that describes the Swedish inflation problem, because that is the number the Riksbank's own Executive Board quotes to each other in the minutes. Every stance that depends on inflation depends on that choice, and if the adjustment is wrong the Inflation and Growth and Guidance factors are both wrong with it.

Interpretive choice - which unemployment rate. Three Swedish unemployment measures were current at the valuation date: the Labour Force Survey seasonally adjusted trend at 8.7 per cent, registered unemployment at 6.5 per cent and the register-based BAS measure at 5.1 per cent. The macro comparison table uses 8.7 per cent because it is the ILO-consistent measure comparable with the other ten currencies, while the factor analysis discusses all three, because the gap between them is the single largest source of disagreement about how much slack the Swedish economy actually has.

RESEARCH-SOURCED BUT NOT SEPARATELY CITED - the schema caps the citation list at 40 entries, which is fewer than the number of distinct sources this build used. The following figures come from the run's Phase 1 research checkpoint, are recorded there with full URLs and access dates, and are named here with their publishers so that provenance is traceable even though they carry no bracketed reference: the S&P 500 close of 7,686.14 and the Dow close of 53,885.10 (Washington Post and Barchart); the S&P 500 year-to-date figure of approximately 12.5 per cent (ChartRow); the OMX Stockholm 30 level of 3,270.78, its 26.89 per cent twelve-month gain and its 3,349.20 all-time high (Trading Economics, Sweden stock market page); Federal Reserve total assets of 6.731 trillion dollars and the IORB rate of 3.65 per cent (FRED, series WALCL and IORB); the end of quantitative tightening in December 2025 (MacroRadar, a secondary source); NBSK pulp at 1,770 dollars a tonne list and 880 to 920 dollars spot (Fastmarkets); copper at 6.62 dollars a pound, aluminium at 3,278.15 dollars a tonne and iron ore at 95.84 dollars a tonne (Trading Economics and Rio Times); AP7's approximate SEK 1.5 trillion size, its unhedged currency policy and its 2025 return of 4.2 per cent against 27.3 per cent in 2024, and the AP1 to AP4 statutory currency-exposure limit and the officially commissioned evaluation of it (AP7's own site and IPE); Swedish defence spending of 2.8 per cent of GDP in 2026 rising to a stated 3.5 per cent by 2030, the SEK 26.6 billion appropriation increase and defence exports of approximately 0.7 per cent of GDP (Government of Sweden and Bank of America); the ECB's December 2025 findings on SEB and Swedbank Baltic internal models and the EUR 1.24 million fine, and Baltic GDP growth of 2.9 per cent in 2026 (Investing.com and SEB); Arbetsformedlingen registered unemployment of 6.5 per cent and 350,176 persons for July 2026 (Arbetsformedlingen); and the SEB fiscal estimates of approximately SEK 80 billion of reforms and SEK 130 billion of total expansion, and general government net lending of minus 2.4 and minus 2.2 per cent of GDP (SEB Nordic Outlook, 27 January 2026).

FLAGGED BY VERIFICATION - Brent settlement conflict. The 94.65 dollar Brent settlement for 1 September 2026 is carried by the cited source and was confirmed verbatim there, but a second vendor quotes Brent at 91.28 dollars for the same date, a gap of roughly 3.4 dollars. The dossier retains 94.65 because it is the sourced settlement rather than an intraday scrape, and because the WTI leg of 90.22 dollars is independently corroborated, but the level is best available and flagged. Nothing in the External Balance stance turns on the difference: both sources have Brent above 90 dollars and sharply higher on the day.

FLAGGED BY VERIFICATION - Riksbank Financial Markets Survey staleness. The survey used as the only official Swedish positioning and FX-liquidity input was fielded between 30 March and 17 April 2026 and is roughly 137 days old at the valuation date, far outside the 30-day tactical freshness window and outside the 60-day strategic one. It is used in Factor 3 and Factor 4 on both horizons, and the confidence on both tactical readings has been reduced to reflect it - Factor 3 tactical to 53 and Factor 4 tactical to 38. Both factors are Neutral, so neither contributes to either weighted score.

FLAGGED BY VERIFICATION - current account, three measures on three bases. Statistics Sweden's own first-quarter 2026 release states the current account at 6.1 per cent of GDP; the cached point-in-time OECD vintage carried in the macro comparison table for cross-currency consistency with the other ten dossiers in this cycle is 4.5 per cent; and the NIER forecasts 4.7 per cent for calendar 2026. The three are not contradictory - they are a single quarter, a four-quarter OECD vintage and an annual forecast respectively - but they are not interchangeable, and the macro table deliberately uses the cached vintage so that the eleven rows are computed the same way.

FLAGGED BY VERIFICATION - additional stale inputs used inside their factors. The Riksgalden Central Government Borrowing report of 28 May 2026 is 96 days old and is used in Factor 8 tactically as well as strategically; the Riksbank and NIER June 2026 forecast rounds are 77 days old and are the most recent available, with the next Riksbank round due 24 September 2026; the Medlingsinstitutet wage figure has a June 2026 reference month, 63 days old, although it was published on 31 August; and the register-based BAS unemployment rate of 5.1 per cent and the employment rate of 81.8 per cent likewise carry a June reference month. The Riksbank reserve-allocation decision cited for the Riksbank's own krona view is dated 3 December 2025 and took effect on 1 January 2026, so it is 272 days old and is used only as a statement of standing policy, not as a current observation.

FLAGGED BY VERIFICATION - citation 26 is a landing page. The Riksgalden Central Government Borrowing 2026:1 entry points at the publication's landing page, which links to but does not itself contain the deficit, issuance and debt figures; those figures are carried verbatim in the accompanying press release, which is citation 25 and is referenced alongside 26 everywhere the fiscal numbers appear.

VERIFICATION RESULT. This dossier was fact-checked by two independent adversarial subagents before publication. Every direct quotation from the Riksbank's 19 August 2026 minutes was confirmed verbatim and correctly attributed; the central inflation claim - CPIF 0.7 per cent measured against approximately 2.2 per cent adjusted for temporary fiscal measures - was confirmed four separate times in the minutes and against the Statistics Sweden release, and a secondary source reporting CPIF at 3.0 per cent was positively identified as the July 2025 figure; all Riksbank SWEA API series, the Riksgalden fiscal block, second-quarter GDP, the NIER survey, the manufacturing PMI, the trade and current account data, the election date and the absence of CME krona options were confirmed. Corrections applied after verification: the Swedish 2-year yield restated as 2.53 per cent for 31 August rather than 2.53 per cent for 1 September, with the 2s10s curve restated at plus 58.7 basis points on matched closes; July goods exports and imports restated at plus 4.0 and plus 6.0 per cent; the manufacturing PMI input-price prior restated at 67.1; the Dutch TTF level restated as about 70 euros with a 70.49 euro intraday high; a pip-arithmetic error corrected from 2.6 to 262 pips; a dead Statistics Sweden foreign-trade URL replaced with the live product page; uncited German PMI flash and consensus detail removed; and the tactical weighted-score commentary corrected to include the Fiscal contribution of plus 0.0208.
